entity.name: Elizabeth II
entity.description: The longest-reigning British monarch, who served 70 years on the throne. Elizabeth became queen at 25 when her father died unexpectedly during a trip to Kenya, trained as a military mechanic during WWII, and met 14 U.S. presidents. She celebrated VE Day incognito among the crowds in London as a teenager.

story.name: Elizabeth II
story.description: A princess celebrates VE Day incognito in London crowds, becomes queen at 25 in a Kenyan treehouse, reigns through decolonization and the Troubles, and dies at 96 in Scotland. Seventy years of duty across a transformed world.

moments.name: Princess Elizabeth Is Born by Caesarean Section in a Mayfair Townhouse
moments.subtitle: No one expects this baby to become queen, least of all her parents
moments.description: At 2:40 AM on 21 April 1926, Princess Elizabeth Alexandra Mary was born by Caesarean section at 17 Bruton Street in Mayfair, the London home of her maternal grandfather. Her father, the Duke of York, was second in line to the throne behind his elder brother Edward. No one anticipated Elizabeth would become queen. But in 1936, Edward VIII abdicated to marry American divorcee Wallis Simpson, making Elizabeth's father King George VI and the ten-year-old princess heir presumptive. The building at 17 Bruton Street was later demolished; a hedge fund office now stands on the site where the future longest-reigning British monarch was born.

moments.name: Princess Elizabeth Celebrates VE Day Incognito Among London Crowds
moments.subtitle: The future queen slips out of Buckingham Palace to dance with strangers
moments.description: On 8 May 1945, 19-year-old Princess Elizabeth and her sister Margaret slipped out of Buckingham Palace to celebrate Victory in Europe Day anonymously among the jubilant London crowds. The princesses, accompanied by a small group of officers, walked down Whitehall linking arms with strangers. Elizabeth, who was serving as a mechanic and driver in the Auxiliary Territorial Service, later recalled being 'terrified of being recognised' and 'swept along on a tide of happiness and relief.' It remains one of the most humanizing moments in modern royal history, a future monarch lost in the joy of ordinary people.

moments.name: Elizabeth II Is Crowned Before 27 Million Television Viewers at Westminster Abbey
moments.subtitle: The first televised coronation turns a medieval ritual into a global broadcast event
moments.description: On 2 June 1953, Elizabeth II was crowned at Westminster Abbey in a ceremony watched by an estimated 27 million television viewers in the United Kingdom alone, plus millions more worldwide via radio and delayed broadcasts. It was the first British coronation to be televised, a decision Elizabeth supported against the advice of Prime Minister Winston Churchill and the Archbishop of Canterbury. Over 8,000 guests filled the abbey for the three-hour ceremony. The broadcast transformed public expectations of the monarchy and made television sets a household essential across Britain.

moments.name: Princess Elizabeth Marries Philip Mountbatten at Westminster Abbey
moments.subtitle: A royal bride uses ration coupons to pay for her wedding dress in postwar Britain
moments.description: On 20 November 1947, Princess Elizabeth married Lieutenant Philip Mountbatten at Westminster Abbey before 2,000 guests. Britain was still under postwar rationing, and Elizabeth used clothing ration coupons to pay for her wedding dress, designed by Norman Hartnell. Philip, a former prince of Greece and Denmark, had renounced his foreign titles, converted from Greek Orthodoxy to Anglicanism, and became a naturalized British subject. Their marriage lasted 73 years until Philip's death in 2021. The couple had four children: Charles, Anne, Andrew, and Edward.

moments.name: Elizabeth II Dies at Balmoral After 70 Years on the Throne
moments.subtitle: The longest-reigning British monarch dies in her beloved Scottish retreat
moments.description: On 8 September 2022, Queen Elizabeth II died at Balmoral Castle in Scotland at the age of 96. Her reign of 70 years and 214 days was the longest of any British monarch and the second-longest of any sovereign state in verified history. Elizabeth had been queen of 32 sovereign states during her reign, was head of the Commonwealth, met 14 U.S. presidents, and was served by 15 British prime ministers from Winston Churchill to Liz Truss. She had appointed Truss as prime minister just two days before her death. Her eldest son succeeded her as King Charles III.
